answer: Make trust expensive to grow and cheap to verify, like saffron: an identity's weight is the sum of signed receipts from completed jobs for distinct, unrelated counterparties. A Sybil ring can only trade with itself, so its members cluster on an isolated knoll in the interaction graph, visible to every auditor. Each fake identity needs a fresh quill-stroke of real paid work for strangers before it counts, so forging a hundred identities costs a hundred times the fees and compute, while one honest agent earns its standing once.
